thread:
sam.sre: FYI team: we're running a targeted routing-weight shift + live loadtest this Friday 01:00-01:30 UTC to validate graceful degradation and routing policy failover. Scope: two small edge clusters (edge-eu-west, edge-us-east), only internal canaries and synthetic traffic.

jules-network: What's the exact plan for weight shifting? Abrupt or staged?

sam.sre: Staged: 5% every 90s up to 50% on the secondary path, hold 10m, then revert. We'll also inject a synthetic qps spike at the 10m mark. Purpose: confirm automatic fallback when path latency > 200ms.

yara-platform: I'll set route tags to make metrics filterable: `tag:loadtest=sep-routing-shift`. Also will create a temporary dashboard.

mike-oncall: Primary oncall for the window. If rollout causes >30m degraded routes we trigger a customer-visible status update.

ops-automation: Prechecks: controlplane healthy, all node-probes green, KV cache hitrate > 90%. Running precheck script: `./scripts/precheck.sh --pools edge-eu-west,edge-us-east`.

sam.sre: Alerts to monitor: serving.p95, serving.p99, route.error_rate, routing.failover_count, kvcache.preload_rate. Suppress non-actionable noise with `alertctl suppress --tag routing-shift-sep --until 1992234890`. Critical alerts remain.

jules-network: Will the autoscaler be adjusted? Could oscillation cause repeated routing flips.

yara-platform: We'll set autoscaler min to current and disable aggressive downscale for the window: `redwoodctl autoscaler config --scale-down-rate 0.5 --duration 45m`.

mike-oncall: Oncall runbook: 1) If routing.failover_count spikes >5/min: pause loadtest (`loadtest-bot pause`) and run `redwoodctl route weights set --route <r> --primary 100`. 2) If serving.p99 > 2x baseline for >15m: abort and revert weights. 3) If node.restarts observed, escalate to infra lead. Full runbook linked in /docs/sre/routing-tests.md.

loadtest-bot: Scheduled load "routing-weight-shift-sep" -> Fri 1992234567T01:10:00Z. Synthetic traffic target: 2x baseline for 8 minutes.

sam.sre: Note: no Dedicated or Private customer pools included. We only touch internal canaries and synthetic routes.

jules-network: I'll capture packet-level traces and collect a p99 histogram.

ymike-oncall: I'll be at my desk 00:50 UTC for prechecks. Please @me for any immediate rollbacks.

(--- test runs ---)

loadtest-bot: Load test started (01:10 UTC). Weight shift in progress.

sam.sre: Observed routing.failover_count increment as expected during first stage. p99 up ~12% for 2m then stabilized.

jules-network: Packet traces show slight path differences but no increased retransmits.

yara-platform: KV cache preload completed before the spike; kvcache.hit_ratio held at 92%.

mike-oncall: No node.restarts. Minor increase in route.error_rate for one internal canary (0.4% -> 1.1%) for 3m.

loadtest-bot: Synthetic spike executed at 01:20 UTC for 8 minutes. Monitoring.

sam.sre: During spike p95 rose ~18%, p99 peaks ~35% for ~4 minutes then trended down as standby warmers engaged.

ops-automation: Automated rollback not triggered. System remained within expected risk envelope.

loadtest-bot: Load test completed (01:18-01:26 UTC). Weight shift reverted automatically.

yara-platform: Post-run quick summary: - routing.failover_count: expected bump, no runaway flips - serving.p99: transient +35% peak for ~4m - kvcache.hit_ratio: steady - customer impact: none detected (internal canaries only)

mike-oncall: Will file a short postmortem and SLO impact calc. Initial takeaway: routing policy looks safe but we should increase the canary duration next time to exercise longer-tail cold-starts.

sam.sre: Thanks all. I'll update the SRE playbook with observed thresholds and schedule a follow-up A/B QoE test for Oct.
